node.title: Understanding compliance frameworks
node.question: What is a compliance framework and why do organisations use one?
node.canonical_question: What is a compliance framework and why do organisations use one?
summary: Compliance frameworks help organisations manage risk systematically.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: A compliance framework is a structured set of guidelines that helps an organisation align its policies with regulatory requirements.

key_points: Compliance frameworks help organisations manage risk systematically.

node.title: Control-based risk management
node.question: How do control-based frameworks reduce organisational risk?
node.canonical_question: How do control-based frameworks reduce organisational risk?
summary: Controls reduce risk by limiting exposure at defined points in a process.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Control frameworks enumerate checkpoints at which risk can be measured and mitigated.

key_points: Controls reduce risk by limiting exposure at defined points in a process.

node.title: Audit preparation fundamentals
node.question: What general steps should a team take before an external audit?
node.canonical_question: What general steps should a team take before an external audit?
summary: Good audit preparation involves evidence gathering and gap identification.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Teams should collect supporting documentation, map controls to requirements, and run internal pre-checks before an external auditor arrives.

key_points: Good audit preparation involves evidence gathering and gap identification.

node.title: Gap analysis methodology
node.question: How do you perform a gap analysis for a compliance standard?
node.canonical_question: How do you perform a gap analysis for a compliance standard?
summary: Gap analysis compares current state to required state across each control.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: A gap analysis maps each control requirement to current evidence and flags where evidence is missing or insufficient.

key_points: Gap analysis compares current state to required state across each control.

node.title: Continuous improvement cycles
node.question: What is a continuous improvement cycle in a compliance context?
node.canonical_question: What is a continuous improvement cycle in a compliance context?
summary: Continuous improvement cycles use audit findings to iteratively close gaps.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: After each audit, identified gaps are prioritised, remediated, and re-tested in the next cycle.

key_points: Continuous improvement cycles use audit findings to iteratively close gaps.

node.title: Evidence collection best practices
node.question: What makes audit evidence reliable and sufficient?
node.canonical_question: What makes audit evidence reliable and sufficient?
summary: Reliable evidence is contemporaneous, attributable, and complete.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Evidence is strongest when it is collected at the time of the controlled activity, tagged to the person responsible, and covers the full scope of the control.

key_points: Reliable evidence is contemporaneous, attributable, and complete.

node.title: Escalation and exception handling
node.question: When should a compliance exception be escalated and how?
node.canonical_question: When should a compliance exception be escalated and how?
summary: Exceptions that cannot be remediated in-cycle require formal escalation.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: An exception is raised when a control cannot be met by the required date. It is escalated to the process owner who logs the risk acceptance or requests a waiver.

key_points: Exceptions that cannot be remediated in-cycle require formal escalation.

node.title: Scope definition for compliance reviews
node.question: How do you define the scope of a compliance review?
node.canonical_question: How do you define the scope of a compliance review?
summary: Scope definition identifies which systems, processes, and data are in-scope.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Scope is bounded by data classification, system ownership, and the specific standard being assessed.

key_points: Scope definition identifies which systems, processes, and data are in-scope.

node.title: Common compliance mistakes
node.question: What are the most common mistakes teams make during compliance reviews?
node.canonical_question: What are the most common mistakes teams make during compliance reviews?
summary: Common mistakes include incomplete evidence and undocumented exceptions.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: Teams frequently fail to maintain contemporaneous records, leaving auditors with reconstructed evidence that carries less weight.

key_points: Common mistakes include incomplete evidence and undocumented exceptions.

node.title: Roles in a compliance programme
node.question: Who owns compliance activities in a typical organisation?
node.canonical_question: Who owns compliance activities in a typical organisation?
summary: Compliance ownership is distributed across process owners, a central function, and executive sponsors.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.body_md: The central compliance function sets the framework; process owners gather evidence; executive sponsors approve risk acceptance.

key_points: Compliance ownership is distributed across process owners, a central function, and executive sponsors.
